newsitem.title: USA: Government to charge RJR on "Joe Camel" ads.
newsitem.headline: Government to charge RJR on "Joe Camel" ads.

text.p: The government will charge R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co. with unfair advertising because of its "Joe Camel" ads, the Federal Trade Commission said on Wednesday.
The FTC offered no details, except to say that it would hold a news conference at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) to provide details of its decision.
The FTC voted 3-2 in 1994 not to act against the "Joe Camel" campaign, but left the door open to future action.
Since then, the FTC has told R.J. Reynolds that it has new evidence on the effects of the ad campaign, sources said.
On March 26, R.J. Reynolds issued a statement saying: "There has been no new substantive research reported since June 1994 that would change the results the FTC found then."
R.J. Reynolds had no immediate comment on the latest action by the FTC.
